segments.text: Als „Deklination“ bezeichnet man die Beugung bzw. Flexion von Substantiven, Adjektiven, Artikeln und Pronomen.
Das Besondere an Substantiven ist, dass sie als einzige Wortart das Genus in sich tragen.
Das Besondere an Adjektiven ist, dass sie entweder stark, schwach oder gemischt dekliniert werden.

name: Deutsche Welle · Deutsch lernen – Grammatik（A Word order）

segments.text: Two main clauses can be joined by a coordinating conjunction, such as und, aber or sondern.
Subordinate clauses cannot stand on their own. They always require a main clause to which they refer (implicitly or explicitly).
Note: in the subordinate clause the conjugated verb always goes to the end of the clause.
The grammar of the German language is quite similar to that of the other Germanic languages.
German grammar differs from that of English in that it has, among other things, cases and gender in nouns and a strict verb-second word order in main clauses.
There are three genders and four cases, and verbs are conjugated for person and number.
German sentence structure is similar to other Germanic languages in its use of V2 word order.
